chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
All those possessing fangs from the predatory animals, and claws from the birds, are forbidden.

key_terms.السباع: Predatory beasts/wild carnivores — encompassing lions, wolves, foxes, dogs and similar animals
key_terms.الطير: Birds — here referring specifically to raptors and other predatory birds
key_terms.حرام: Forbidden/prohibited — categorically impermissible for consumption in Islamic law
key_terms.ذو ناب: One possessing fangs/canine teeth — the defining characteristic of carnivorous predatory mammals
key_terms.مخلب: Claw/talon — specifically the sharp hooked claws of birds of prey

ai.seo_question: Which animals are forbidden to eat according to Imam al-Sadiq in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) enunciates a comprehensive jurisprudential principle: all predatory animals equipped with fangs (such as lions, wolves, and dogs) and all birds possessing talons (such as eagles, hawks, and falcons) are prohibited (haram) for consumption. This concise ruling provides a clear distinguishing criterion for permissible and forbidden animal flesh within Islamic dietary law, applicable to the Muslim community in Imam al-Sadiq's time and beyond.
